q: What were net sales and gross margin by year?

attempts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', order_date) AS order_year, ROUND(SUM(net_sales), 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(SUM(gross_profit) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(net_sales), 0), 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM fct_sales GROUP BY strftime('%Y', order_date) ORDER BY order_year

answer: Net sales grew each year, from $866,281 in 2023 to $1,228,157 in 2024 and $1,775,968 in 2025. Gross margin stayed essentially flat at 51.9% in 2023 and 2024, then 52.0% in 2025.
assumption: Gross margin is shown as a percentage of net sales, per calendar year of order_date.

q: Which 5 categories made the most gross profit in 2025?

attempts.sql: SELECT p.category AS category, ROUND(SUM(s.gross_profit), 2) AS gross_profit FROM fct_sales s JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id = s.product_id WHERE strftime('%Y', s.order_date) = '2025' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY SUM(s.gross_profit) DESC LIMIT 5

answer: Outerwear & Coats led 2025 gross profit at $126,716, followed by Jeans ($92,424), Sweaters ($68,655), Suits & Sport Coats ($64,109) and Swim ($51,414). Together these five categories made $403,318 in gross profit, with returned and cancelled items counted as $0 profit.
assumption: Gross profit is SUM(gross_profit) over 2025 order dates; returned and cancelled items contribute 0 profit.

q: Which traffic source brings the highest average order value?

attempts.sql: SELECT c.traffic_source AS traffic_source, ROUND(SUM(s.net_sales) / COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM fct_sales s JOIN dim_customer c ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE s.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') GROUP BY c.traffic_source ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC

answer:
Display brings the highest average order value at $91.22, followed by Search ($86.65) and Organic ($85.43). Email ($83.34) and Facebook ($82.60) are lowest, so the gap from top to bottom is $8.62.

This covers 2023-2025 and excludes cancelled and returned items.
assumption: Computed AOV per traffic source across all years (2023-2025), using only items that are not cancelled or returned.

q: How did the return rate change month by month in 2025?

attempts.sql: SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS order_month, ROUND(SUM(status = 'Returned') * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(status <> 'Cancelled'), 0), 1) AS return_rate_pct FROM fct_sales WHERE strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025' GROUP BY substr(order_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY order_month

answer: The return rate stayed in a narrow band of 10.5% to 12.9% through 2025, with no clear trend. It peaked in February at 12.9% and bottomed in August at 10.5%, then settled around 12.0%-12.3% from September to December. January started at 11.5% and December ended at 12.0%, a net rise of 0.5 points.
assumption: Months are based on order_date, and return rate uses the standard definition (returned items divided by non-cancelled items).

q: Which brands have the worst return rate, with at least 500 items sold?

attempts.sql: SELECT p.brand AS brand, SUM(f.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned')) AS items_sold, SUM(f.status = 'Returned') AS returned_items, ROUND(SUM(f.status = 'Returned') * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(f.status <> 'Cancelled'), 0), 1) AS return_rate_pct FROM fct_sales f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id = f.product_id GROUP BY p.brand HAVING SUM(f.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned')) >= 500 ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC LIMIT 10

answer: Levi's has the worst return rate at 13.3% (87 returned items against 568 sold), followed by Tommy Hilfiger at 12.7% and Hanes at 12.1%. Among brands with at least 500 items sold, the top 10 range from 10.6% (Quiksilver) to 13.3%, across 2023-2025. Allegra K has the highest volume of the group, with 2,272 items sold and 293 returns (11.4%).
assumption: Across all years (2023-2025), 'items sold' means non-cancelled, non-returned items per the metric definition, and I show the top 10 brands by return rate.

q: What share of 2025 net sales came from the top 10 brands?

attempts.sql: WITH brand_sales AS (SELECT p.brand AS brand, SUM(f.net_sales) AS brand_net_sales FROM fct_sales f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id = f.product_id WHERE strftime('%Y', f.order_date) = '2025' GROUP BY p.brand), ranked AS (SELECT brand, brand_net_sales, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY brand_net_sales DESC) AS brand_rank FROM brand_sales) SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN brand_rank <= 10 THEN brand_net_sales ELSE 0 END), 2) AS top_10_brands_net_sales, ROUND(SUM(brand_net_sales), 2) AS total_net_sales, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN brand_rank <= 10 THEN brand_net_sales ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(brand_net_sales), 0), 1) AS top_10_brands_share_pct FROM ranked

answer: The top 10 brands generated 13.5% of 2025 net sales, or $239,552 out of $1,775,968 total. Brands are ranked by 2025 net sales, so sales are spread widely across many brands rather than concentrated in a few.
assumption: Top 10 brands are ranked by 2025 net sales; share is relative to total 2025 net sales across all brands.

q: Which country's customers spend the most per order?

attempts.sql: WITH items AS (SELECT CASE WHEN c.country = 'España' THEN 'Spain' ELSE c.country END AS country, s.order_id, s.net_sales FROM fct_sales s JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE s.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned')) SELECT country, ROUND(SUM(net_sales) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM items GROUP BY country ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC LIMIT 10

answer: Japan's customers spend the most per order at $87 on average (net sales of $96,179 across 1,100 orders), but the lead is slim. France ($87) and the United States ($87) are within about $0.50, and the top 10 countries all fall between $84 and $87 per order. Cancelled and returned items are excluded.
assumption: Spend per order is average order value (net sales per order, excluding cancelled and returned items) over all years, with 'España' merged into 'Spain'; top 10 shown with order counts for context.

q: How many customers placed more than one order?

attempts.sql: WITH cust_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count FROM fct_sales WHERE status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers FROM cust_orders WHERE order_count > 1

answer: 8,841 customers placed more than one order. This counts distinct orders with non-cancelled items across the full 2023-2025 period.
assumption: Orders are distinct order_ids on non-cancelled items, across the full 2023-2025 period.

q: By how much did net sales grow from 2024 to 2025?

attempts.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_2024, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_2025, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_growth_usd, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END), 0), 1) AS net_sales_growth_pct FROM fct_sales WHERE strftime('%Y', order_date) IN ('2024', '2025')

answer: Net sales grew by $547,811 (44.6%) from 2024 to 2025, rising from $1,228,157 to $1,775,968.
assumption: Growth is reported both as absolute USD change and percent change in net sales, 2025 vs 2024.

q: Which distribution center ships fastest, and which slowest?

attempts.sql: SELECT p.distribution_center AS distribution_center, ROUND(AVG(s.days_to_ship), 2) AS avg_days_to_ship, COUNT(*) AS shipped_items FROM fct_sales s JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id = s.product_id WHERE s.days_to_ship IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.distribution_center ORDER BY avg_days_to_ship ASC

answer: New Orleans LA ships fastest at 0.5 average days to ship (4,008 items), while Philadelphia PA is slowest at 0.58 days (5,193 items). The gap is small: all 10 centers fall within 0.08 days of each other.
assumption: Average days to ship per distribution center over all shipped items, sorted so the fastest is first and the slowest last.

q: How many orders were cancelled in 2025, and what share is that?

attempts.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled' THEN order_id END) AS cancelled_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled' THEN order_id END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 0), 1) AS cancelled_order_share_pct, SUM(status = 'Cancelled') AS cancelled_items, ROUND(SUM(status = 'Cancelled') * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS item_cancellation_rate_pct FROM fct_sales WHERE strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025'

answer: In 2025, 4,272 of 27,598 orders were cancelled, a share of 15.5%. An order counts as cancelled if it has at least one cancelled item. At the item level, 6,095 items were cancelled, a rate of 15.3%.
assumption: An order counts as cancelled if it has at least one cancelled item. The share is cancelled orders over all 2025 orders, and the standard item-level cancellation rate is included for reference.
